key_insight: A local two-stage language model pipeline can accurately find hepatocellular carcinoma cases and extract structured histopathology variables from German free-text reports.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support privacy-preserving registry curation and pathology quality control without sending sensitive patient data outside the institution.
method: Stage 1: a lightweight gatekeeper model screened 2,864 reports to identify confirmed HCC cases.
Stage 2: a higher-capacity model extracted 15 predefined variables into JSON, including staging, grade, vascular invasion, and immunohistochemistry.
All processing ran locally within a secure institutional network.
evidence_signal: The best pipeline showed zero classification errors in cohort detection and near-perfect extraction performance, with the 31B Gemma 4 model reporting Macro F1 > 0.99 against expert reference annotations.
watch_item: Performance was measured on expert-curated reference data, so real-world deployment still needs checks for unseen report styles, rare edge cases, and ongoing quality monitoring.
paper_title: Large Language Models for Structured Information Extraction from German Histopathology Reports - Hepatocellular Carcinoma
